title: Field Trip
cn: 第 5 集 · 实地考察
novel: Marshall decided to take matters into his own hands at work. He was tired of his boss [[ignoring|ignore]] his ideas about the environment. Marshall [[believed|believe]] that his company should do more to protect nature. He [[gathered|gather]] all his courage and [[confronted|confront]] his boss directly. His boss was [[shocked|shock]] by Marshall's boldness but [[listened|listen]] to what he had to say. Meanwhile, Ted took his architecture class on a [[field trip|field trip]] that went terribly wrong. He wanted to show his students a real [[construction|construction]] site. He thought it would be [[educational|educational]] and [[inspiring|inspire]]. However, the site was [[dangerous|dangerous]] and not ready for visitors. Ted had not [[obtained|obtain]] the proper [[permission|permission]] to bring his class there. The [[foreman|foreman]] was angry and asked them to leave immediately. Ted felt [[embarrassed|embarrass]] in front of his students. He had tried to do something [[creative|creative]] but it had [[backfired|backfire]]. His students were confused about why their teacher had brought them to a closed site. Ted [[apologized|apologize]] to the class and [[promised|promise]] to make it up to them. Marshall's boss actually [[considered|consider]] his ideas about going green. It was a small victory, but Marshall felt proud of himself for speaking up.

ignore.en: to pay no attention to something

confront.en: to deal with a problem directly

field trip.en: a trip for students to learn outside

inspire.en: to give someone ideas or energy

foreman.en: a person in charge of workers

promise.en: to say you will do something
